title: Group comparisons and measurement invariance
summary: Comparing paths between groups requires a formal test of the difference and evidence that the constructs are measured the same way in each group.

body.text: [[multigroup-analysis]] asks whether a path differs between groups, for example between countries. Two facts must hold before differences can be interpreted. First, the difference itself must be tested: one group having a significant path and the other not does not show that the paths differ (Gelman & Stern 2006). Permutation tests and PLS-MGA are common procedures in PLS-SEM (Sarstedt et al. 2011).

Second, the constructs must mean the same in each group: [[measurement-invariance]]. For composites, the [[micom]] procedure (Henseler et al. 2016) checks configural invariance, compositional invariance (composite scores built with each group's weights correlate almost perfectly) and the equality of composite means and variances. Without it, a different path may reflect a different construct rather than a different effect.
SEM Lab does not run MICOM, permutation tests or PLS-MGA yet; they are planned. Estimating separate models per group is possible, but comparing them by eye is not a test.
body.title: Not available in SEM Lab

mistake.title: "Significant in group A, not in group B, so the groups differ"
mistake.text: Two p values on either side of .05 can come from nearly identical estimates. Test the difference, and establish invariance first.

checks.question: A path is .30 (p = .01) for women and .22 (p = .08) for men. What can you conclude?

options.text: Nothing yet about a difference; you need a test of the difference and evidence of invariance.
options.feedback: Correct. The estimates are close, and the difference has not been tested.

options.text: The effect exists only for women.
options.feedback: A p value of .08 is not evidence of no effect, and the two estimates are similar.
Significance in one group and not in the other is not a significant difference (Gelman & Stern 2006).

checks.question: Why is measurement invariance assessed before comparing structural paths?

options.text: Because path differences are only interpretable if the constructs have the same meaning and composition in each group.

options.feedback: Invariance testing is about comparability, not power.

options.text: Because the software requires it to run.
options.feedback: Models can be estimated without it; the issue is interpretation.
